row: QA-09 (date vocab), QA-10 (time vocab), QA-11 (recurrence vocab), QA-12 (priority vocab)
method: each term typed ALONE into a freshly-cleared draft; data-match-id read back, both apps
reference_date: 2026-09-11 (Friday, per system clock; confirmed by 'today' and 'friday' both resolving to 2026-09-11 / '11 Sep')

next week.DIVERGENT: Todoist resolves 'next week' to Mon 14 Sep (start of next week); meologue resolves it to Fri 18 Sep (today+7). Different day of week entirely, not just format.

12/25.DIVERGENT: Todoist recognises '12/25' as 25 Dec; meologue does NOT recognise it at all (hasSpan: false) - a real parity gap, not a formatting difference.

at 5pm.note: Todoist attaches a rolled-forward date (tomorrow, since 5pm today has presumably passed) plus 12h time; meologue's match-id carries only the bare 24h time with no date.

daily.note: Todoist normalises the match-id itself to 'every day'; meologue's match-id stays 'daily' (raw token), though ledger QA-11 states the STORED phrase is normalised to 'every day' downstream - the match-id display differs.

notes: All 20 vocabulary terms were recognised (hasSpan true, data-highlighted-match true) on the meologue side except '12/25', and all 20 were recognised on the Todoist side including '12/25'.

Priority match-id format differs structurally: Todoist uses a bare digit ('1'-'4'), meologue uses a letter+digit UI label ('P1'-'P4'). Neither is the internally-inverted stored value (P1 stored as priority 4) - both surfaces expose a UI-facing number here.

Time-only phrases differ structurally: Todoist's match-id bundles a resolved calendar date with the time ('12 Sep 5:00 PM'); meologue's match-id is time-only ('17:00'), with no date component visible in the identifier.
